name: Creamy Garlic Herb Wine Pork Chops

ingredients.buy: 14 thin-cut boneless pork chops (about 4 1/4 oz / 120 g each, roughly 3 3/4 lb)
14 tbsp (7 for searing, 7 for the sauce)
7 tsp (3 1/2 for the dredge, 3 1/2 for the sauce)
salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste (about 1 tsp salt)

prose.intro_html: Pork chops get a bad name because most people cook them to the texture of a hockey puck. This is the fix. You dredge the chops in seasoned almond flour, sear them fast so they stay tender, then build a creamy garlic, herb, and white wine pan sauce right in the same skillet and let the two finish together. No breadcrumbs, no flour, no gluten anywhere in it. Built at 14 servings it runs about {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein a serving, with under 10 grams of carbs. That is a restaurant-style creamy pork chop that still lands inside a low-carb week.
shop_smart: Fourteen thin-cut boneless pork chops are the backbone. That is roughly three and three-quarter pounds, one chop per serving, and it is where most of the money and all of the protein live. Reach for the big family pack of boneless chops instead of the small trays so you are paying for pork, not packaging. Thin-cut is the move here, because a thin chop sears in three or four minutes a side and stays tender instead of drying out.

Almond flour is the dredge, and it is what keeps this gluten free. You need about a cup and change of blanched almond flour to coat all fourteen chops. This is not a spot for regular all-purpose flour, because the whole point of this dish is a low-carb, gluten-free crust. Blanched almond flour lives on the baking aisle near the other specialty flours.

Heavy cream and a splash of dry white wine make the sauce. You need about a cup and three-quarters of cream and the same of wine. Any dry white you would actually drink works here, so skip the bottle labeled cooking wine. The cream is what carries the sauce, so buy the real heavy cream and not a light version.

Parmesan thickens the sauce and seasons it at the same time. Grate in about one and three-quarter cups, which is roughly seven ounces. It melts into the cream and wine and pulls the whole thing together, no cornstarch or roux needed.

Garlic, a lemon, and fresh thyme are the flavor. A head of garlic for the seven cloves, one small lemon for the juice, and a little bundle of fresh thyme. Fresh thyme is worth hunting for here since it is the herb the sauce is built around, but if your store only carries the packaged herbs, grab the smallest one.

Butter and three pantry seasonings round it out. Butter to sear in and to start the sauce, plus garlic powder, onion powder, and Italian seasoning for the dredge and the sauce. These are backbone staples you most likely already have, so they barely move the cart.
make_it: Weigh your empty skillet and write the number down. You will use it at the end to split this into 14 even servings by weight instead of eyeballing every container.

In a large bowl, whisk together the almond flour, garlic powder, onion powder, and 3 1/2 teaspoons of the Italian seasoning. Season the pork chops all over with salt and pepper, then dredge each one thoroughly in the almond flour mixture.

Heat 7 tablespoons of the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Working in batches so the pan is not crowded, add the chops and sear about 3 to 4 minutes a side, six to eight minutes total. Cook the first side on medium-high, then drop the heat to medium for the second side. Move the chops to a plate and cover to keep warm.
Return the skillet to the heat and add the remaining 7 tablespoons of butter and the minced garlic. Cook about 1 to 2 minutes over medium heat until the garlic is fragrant.
Pour in the white wine and squeeze in the lemon juice, then add the chicken broth and the heavy cream. Bring the sauce up to a boil, then lower the heat.

Stir in the fresh thyme leaves and the remaining 3 1/2 teaspoons of Italian seasoning, then season with salt and pepper. Add the grated parmesan and simmer 2 to 3 minutes until the sauce thickens. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Reduce the heat to low and return the chops and any collected juices to the pan. Spoon the sauce over them and reheat on low 2 to 3 minutes until the chops are cooked through.
Weigh the full pan and subtract the empty weight from Step 1 to get the cooked total. Divide by 14 and give each container one chop and an even share of the creamy herb sauce, aiming for that weight.
prose.portion_html: Set the full pan on your scale and subtract the empty weight you wrote down in Step 1 to get the cooked total. Divide that number by 14. Each container gets one pork chop and an even spoonful of the creamy garlic herb sauce, landing near {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.
prose.cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a serving (at everyday cost) for a creamy pork chop that tastes like it came off a restaurant menu. The pork and the cream carry it; the wine, the parmesan, and the fresh thyme just make it taste expensive.

head.description: Creamy garlic herb wine pork chops for meal prep: almond-flour-dredged pork chops seared and finished in a creamy white wine and parmesan pan sauce, built for 14 servings. About {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein per serving, with under 10 grams of carbs.
head.keywords: creamy pork chops, low carb pork chops, gluten free pork chops, garlic herb wine sauce, low carb meal prep, high protein pork dinner
steps: Whisk the almond flour with the garlic powder, onion powder, and half the Italian seasoning, then season and dredge the pork chops.
Sear the chops in butter about 3 to 4 minutes a side, then set them aside.
Cook the garlic in more butter, then add the wine, lemon juice, chicken broth, and heavy cream and bring to a boil.
Stir in the thyme, the rest of the Italian seasoning, and the parmesan and simmer until the sauce thickens.
Return the chops to the sauce and reheat on low until cooked through.
Weigh the pan, subtract the empty weight, and divide across 14 containers.
